ground_truth.location: Table 3, Days outside last week, Born before 1955, column (3) +/-45
ground_truth.context: Table 3 ("Effects of Curfew on Mobility Outcomes"), column (3). Regression discontinuity estimate of the effect of being born before December 1955 (the cohorts subject to Turkey's 65+ curfew) on the number of days the respondent went outside last week.  OLS of the outcome on the treatment indicator and a linear function of the running variable (months between the respondent's month-year of birth and the December 1955 threshold) fit separately on each side of the threshold, uniform kernel, sample restricted to respondents born within 45 months of the threshold (the Imbens- Kalyanaraman optimal bandwidth for this outcome).  Controls: month of birth fixed effects, province fixed effects, surveyor fixed effects, and indicators for education level, ethnicity and gender. Sample: respondents of the authors' phone survey of 59- to 70-year-olds in urban Turkey (late May to early July 2020). Standard errors clustered at the month-year of birth cohort.  The entry is the "Born before 1955" coefficient.

ground_truth.unit: standard deviations of the mental distress index
ground_truth.location: Table 4, Mental distress index, Born before 1955, column (3) +/-45
ground_truth.context: Table 4 ("Effects of Curfew on Mental Health Outcomes"), column (3). Reduced-form RD estimate of the effect of being born before December 1955 on the mental distress index, with the Table 3 specification (linear in the running variable on each side, uniform kernel, 45-month bandwidth, month of birth, province and surveyor fixed effects, education, ethnicity and gender indicators, SEs clustered by month-year of birth).  The index follows Anderson (2008) over all 20 SRQ-20 items (binary symptoms within the last four weeks): each item is demeaned and divided by the control group's (born after the threshold) standard deviation, the items are combined with weights from the inverse of their covariance matrix, and the index is scaled to mean 0 and standard deviation 1 in the control group; higher values mean more distress.  The entry is the "Born before 1955" coefficient.
